title: How RETINA measures the complexity of retinal blood vessels
description: A plain-language walkthrough of RETINA's pipeline: from a fundus photograph to a fractal dimension, local measurements and a deviation index.
lede: A retinal photograph shows a branching network of blood vessels. Changes in that branching can be hard to judge by eye. RETINA turns the network into numbers, using a few steps that each have a clear mathematical meaning.

blocks.text: RETINA first resizes the image and works on its green channel. It improves local contrast with CLAHE (contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalisation) and smooths noise with a Gaussian blur. Black-hat morphology and a threshold then separate vessels from background, giving a binary map in which each pixel is either vessel or not.

The global fractal dimension, D, describes how completely the vessels fill the plane. RETINA covers the vessel map with square boxes of side ε and counts how many boxes, N(ε), contain at least one vessel pixel. It repeats this for smaller and smaller boxes.

For a network that fills space more fully, the count grows faster as the boxes shrink. D is the slope of the straight line fitted to ln N(ε) against ln(1/ε), and RETINA reports the fit quality (R²) alongside it. A simple line has D = 1 and a completely filled plane has D = 2, so a branching network falls between them.
As an arithmetic illustration only: if halving the box size multiplied the count by 3, the slope would be log₂ 3, about 1.58.

sections.title: 3. Looking at the network region by region

blocks.text: One number for the whole image can hide differences between regions. RETINA divides the vessel map into a 4×4 grid of 16 regions. For each region i it records the vessel density Pᵢ = Vᵢ / Aᵢ (vessel pixels over region area) and a local box-counting dimension αᵢ.
The multifractal spread, Δα = α<sub>max</sub> − α<sub>min</sub>, summarises how uneven the complexity is across the retina.

A measurement means more when compared with something. RETINA builds its healthy reference, D<sub>H</sub> and Δα<sub>H</sub>, from healthy images the user uploads. No reference values are fixed in the code. The deviations and the final index are then:
A higher MAI means the vessel network departs further from the healthy reference. Without any reference images the app still reports D and Δα, and it withholds FD, MD and MAI.

items: Every number is computed once in Python. The browser animation only plays back stored values and never recomputes them.
A Mathematics page shows each formula with the values from the current image substituted in.

Optional extras stay separate from the core measurements: a ROC / Youden's J cutoff from the user's own labelled analyses, and an experimental Random Forest trained on the computed features. Neither changes how D, Δα, FD, MD or MAI are calculated.
RETINA is a research prototype for study and teaching, not a clinical diagnostic.

blocks.text: The next steps are to evaluate the index on a larger labelled dataset, report classification metrics, and benchmark the MAI against established vascular measures.
